text:
Prose | Red Antler
Arnaud Plas and Paul Michaux had a vision for a haircare company where every product is made-to-order. We helped create the Prose brand from the ground up to showcase the superiority of products made just for you. Amidst many brands claiming to address specific needs, we had to demonstrate the specialness of Prose’s approach, starting with the name which signals a new narrative. We helped design the online diagnostic that determines each formulation, and created a system that showcases your results on the packaging itself, highlighting the range of factors that influence every product. Art direction romances quality ingredients and luscious hair, blending luxury with precision. After a few years of growth, we worked with Prose on a national awareness campaign that celebrates the benefits of “hyper custom haircare.”

text:
Google Fiber | Red Antler
The situation
No one loves their internet service provider. Overplayed marketing and underwhelming service have led consumers to seriously distrust them. But Google Fiber is genuinely better, faster, and more reliable. It just needed a brand platform that would put the difference between it and its competition into stark relief.
The solution
People love the internet. They just hate how they get it. So we stripped away all the things that have been dragging it down - the opaque pricing, the technical jargon, and bombastic claims - to just deliver the internet we’ve all been promised: pure, purposeful, and playfully human. Now doesn’t that sound refreshing?

openGraph.content: The dating app designed to be deleted. Brand, Campaign, and Content Production by Red Antler.

text:
Hinge | Red Antler
Hinge first approached us with a simple yet seemingly elusive goal: pull away from the competition and be the dating app where good people can make meaningful connections. We evolved the brand working side-by-side with the Hinge team as they rebuilt the interface, moving away from swiping and snap judgements to a more human experience. Hinge was then acquired by Match Group, and it was time to tell the world that Hinge wants to get you off the apps and into a real relationship. We created the “Designed to be Deleted” campaign, featuring Hingie, an anthropomorphic version of the app icon who brutally meets its demise every time a couple hits it off. Three versions later, including international expansion and a Gen Z update with Tik Tok creator VO, the campaign has had tremendous impact on Hinge’s business and connections made across the globe.

text:
Jellysmack | Red Antler
Jellysmack, the go-to platform for optimizing creator content and audience reach, first partnered with us in 2018 to develop their brand strategy, identity, and digital experience. At a turning point, they returned in 2021 to create a brand awareness campaign that would meaningfully connect to creators in search of omni-platform growth. Inspired by the infinite expansion made possible through Jellysmack, we developed the campaign concept “Go Bigger.” We brought this to life through a kaleidoscopic motif of mirrors and repetition, casting 11 creators from the Jellysmack community as our focal point. We ultimately created a campaign world that felt so integral, it inversely became a part of the Jellysmack brand identity as a whole.

text:
Bonobos | Red Antler
Bonobos came to Red Antler in need of a hard-hitting brand evolution. Known for its quick wit and tailored fits, the men’s fashion icon needed to win over a younger demographic without alienating long-time customers. To do so, we searched for the commonality between both audiences. Regardless of age, men can find it intimidating to find clothes that fit perfectly—and spur confidence. To inspire our audience to take risks and mix up their wardrobe, we rebranded Bonobos visually and behaviorally around one big idea: Get Changed. Drawing heavily on inspiration from jazz and improv, we went raw and editorial, showcasing its newest collection through stories of real musicians. Both energizing and clever, Bonobos is charming the fashion-curious, nationwide.

text:
Gush | Red Antler
Gush is a new kind of party essential—a scientifically-backed Korean pear juice that helps you seize the night and save the morning after. Even as people make more health-conscious choices about what they put in their bodies, the hangover still feels like an inevitable part of going out. Gush saw an opportunity to reintroduce a centuries-old Korean remedy through a fresh, modern lens, helping people drink smarter without feeling like they’re compromising the fun. Red Antler partnered with the founding team from the very beginning to define the brand, its audience, and how to bring this powerful (and surprisingly delicious) product to market.
We created a brand that feels less like a functional fix and more like a reason to celebrate. From naming and strategy to messaging, visual identity, packaging, and digital design, everything ladders back to the simple idea of getting the most out of your night. We built a world that pairs science with spirit: a pear-inspired palette, euphoric art direction, and copy that turns practical advice into a toast-worthy ritual. Gush makes a smart choice feel like a fun one—and claims its spot as the first thing you reach for before going out.

text:
Bezi | Red Antler
Labneh is a beloved Mediterranean staple, celebrated globally yet largely unfamiliar in the U.S. Bezi set out to change that — to make labneh a thing. Our mission wasn’t just to introduce a new dip, but to build an entirely new snacking category, aiming to unseat hummus as the go-to choice with a brand that’s as approachable as it is crave-worthy. The challenge was to make labneh feel vibrant and inviting for U.S. consumers while remaining authentic to its roots. We crafted a flavor-immersive color palette and a bold, geometric logo to give Bezi a fresh, recognizable look. From a playful mascot inspired by Bezi’s creamy swirls to engaging speech bubbles on the packaging, every detail brings a touch of curiosity and fun, inviting shoppers into the world of labneh. Bezi’s design system is built to expand seamlessly as the line grows, staying true to the brand’s personality. Now turning heads on shelves across New York City’s top grocers, Bezi is redefining healthy snacking and making its mark in American refrigerators.

text:
Levain | Red Antler
Levain Bakery is a New York institution, an integral part of its community, and the home to the world’s absolute best cookies. After more than 20 years, Levain’s founders, Pam and Connie, came to Red Antler with an opportunity to expand its brand — to new storefronts across the world. To bring the heart of Levain forward, we created a delightful world where everything the brand touched became a little more whimsical, a little more fun, and a whole lot sweeter. We began by bringing important details from Levain’s storied history forward - the bright blue of the door on 74th street and the charm of the Upper West Side. From there, we worked to infuse a sense of Pam and Connie’s joy-filled style into every touchpoint, balancing a quirky collage system and eclectic type style with natural textures and a warm approach to interior design.

text:
Allbirds | Red Antler
The footwear industry holds some of the most beloved brands in the world, but it also relies on synthetic materials that are terrible for the environment. When we met the founders, Tim and Joey, they were prototyping their first shoe with the goal of transforming the category by finding new uses for sustainable materials. Our task in launching their wool sneaker was to create a brand that could build a movement. We developed the Allbirds brand from scratch, grounding it in curiosity, and infusing that feeling into everything: an evocative name, flowing logotype, and surprising, dynamic packaging. Each interaction with the brand invites people to join the journey, and the world’s been engaged at every step.

text:
Archer | Red Antler
Archer
Bring out the explorer in all of us
With its electric vertical take-off and landing vehicle (think flying taxi), Archer is tackling traffic and pollution in heavily populated areas and shaping the future of urban air mobility. With an anticipated launch of 2024, Archer will allow people who live outside cities to make trips in 10-15 minutes that previously took an hour or more. We created a brand that builds excitement for launch, while grounding the futuristic vehicle in real life.
We crafted the brand system to hero the exhilarating travel that Archer is making an everyday reality. The wordmark’s sporty aesthetic establishes a sense of momentum and movement, while the organic color palette creates a satisfying tension, evoking calm earth and sky. Conceptual illustrations form patterns that depict elements of flight, like elevation, speed, and propulsion, and arresting messaging infuses energy and drama. With a partnership with United and an order for $1 billion aircraft under Archer’s wing, we’re excited to see the brand propelling forward at full speed.

Abask
Illuminating luxury
Navigating cluttered e-commerce sites to buy home goods can be soulless, encouraging us to fill our carts (and homes) with mass-produced items that feel impersonal. Enter Abask. Founder Tom Chapman set out to create a highly curated digital marketplace for the discerning customer who seeks impeccable design, story, and luxury in equal measure. 
Our challenge was to create a brand world as tactile, nuanced, and storied as the home goods that Abask curates. So we tapped into an elevated, historic sensibility to develop a rich color palette inspired by early 20th-century art, a wordmark that alludes to the weight of a pointed nib pen, and a name that evokes the warm glow of light filling a beautiful space. All came together to underscore Abask’s focus on curation and craft.
Brand Strategy
Research
Brand Identity
Brand Messaging
Art Direction
Packaging Design
The symbol we created for Abask features radiating lines that convey illumination and the aura of beautiful, storied objects. At once evoking the sun, a curatorial gaze, and an exquisite pearl, the symbol reinforces that the most precious things lie in the eye of the beholder.
We employed lines throughout the design system to chart the journey of objects and underscore Abask’s focus on lineage and connection. Embossed lines bring an elevated and tactile quality to the brand.

text:
Henry Rose | Red Antler
The fine fragrance industry uses the term “fragrance” on labels as a catch-all for thousands of under-regulated ingredients. This protects trade secrets while leaving consumers in the dark about what they’re putting on their skin. Michelle Pfeiffer was determined to create the first fully transparent fine fragrance line, setting a new standard for the industry. We partnered with her to develop Henry Rose, a brand that measured up to her mission in a way that felt open and responsible without losing the sensual appeal of fragrance. At every possible touchpoint, including the bottle form itself, we balanced honesty with intrigue, creating a raw brand experience that embraced contrast and tension.

Rebag | Red Antler
Handbag splurges are often justified as “lifelong investments.” But in reality, even our proudest purchases are fated to collect dust in the back of our closets. Unlike a traditional consignment shop, Rebag delivers the opportunity to let go of your bag, get paid immediately, and guiltlessly move onto the next, whenever you’re ready. Through every touchpoint – in-store and online – Rebag needed to establish trust as the authority on handbags while also tapping into the thrill of buying luxury and redefining how we think about ownership. Our system celebrates the endless cycle of newness that Rebag enables by leaning into repetition. We also baked designer names into part of the system, hero-ing Rebag’s strict standards.

text:
Rainbow | Red Antler
Rainbow had a vision to create the first insurance company that actually serves the needs of small businesses, starting with restaurant owners. Our challenge was to build a brand that people would notice, remember, and even love, in a category with painfully low engagement. Without getting too technical, we had to demonstrate to restaurant owners why Rainbow is different. Rainbow’s unique model adapts coverage to a business’s natural fluctuations, and our expressive and bold brand system demonstrates this flexibility, including a custom typeface that morphs and changes. We positioned Rainbow as an uplifting and positive force among the inevitable unpredictability of running a small business, building a world that welcomes ups and downs and looks nothing like traditional insurance.

Furby, the otherworldly icon of the late 90s, had their eyes (and beak) set on making a comeback in 2023. Our challenge was to drive craze for the brand in a contemporary way, shifting it from a toy of yesteryear nostalgia into a modern-day obsession for kids. text:
The Insights That Should Drive Every Campaign in 2025
As consumers navigate a world defined by instability, economic swings, and an endless barrage of information, they’re becoming more selective than ever. Skepticism is at an all-time high, and the brands that break through aren’t the ones making the most noise—they’re the ones proving, time and again, that they’re worth believing in.
With 2025 already shaping up to be another year of volatility, we partnered with leading survey platform Centiment to uncover the factors driving purchasing decisions in this new landscape. The findings reveal a fundamental shift: people are over chasing trends—they’re gravitating toward brands that offer consistency, authenticity, and real value.
For those looking to build deeper connections with their audience, these insights decode the psychology behind consumer trust—and how to earn it.
The Reliability Revolution
Uncertainty has fundamentally rewired consumer psychology. In a world that feels increasingly unstable, people are clinging to what they know and trust. Our data paints a clear picture:
74% trust product claims from established businesses more than newer companies
60% prefer brands that refine existing offerings rather than constantly launching new ones
61% believe older businesses are more likely to genuinely care about their best interests than younger businesses
Even in a category like technology, only about half (52%) of consumers crave innovation
Consumers are done chasing the next big thing—they’re doubling down on brands with a track record of reliability. That means businesses should shift focus from chasing hype to reinforcing their existing value. Highlight longevity, consistency, and proof of performance. Show customers that you're not just here today—you’ll be here tomorrow.
You’re Wrong About GenZ
Growing up in an era of constant hype has made Gen Z naturally skeptical. They don’t just question marketing claims—they can see trendiness itself as a red flag. Compared to older generations, Gen Z is:
10 percentage points more likely to associate trendiness with low quality
12 pp more likely to associate trendiness with insincerity
9 pp more likely to associate trendiness with being overpriced
8 pp more likely to associate trendiness with being impractical
15 pp LESS likely to associate trendiness with innovation
The lesson? Chasing the latest TikTok trend won’t win Gen Z over; trust will. Instead of trying to be “of the moment,” focus on building real credibility. Show them why your brand matters beyond the hype, and how it stands for something deeper than just what’s trending today.
Durability: The New Premium
Premium is no longer about price—it’s about staying power. Consumers are redefining what makes a brand feel high-end or worth their money, and durability is now the ultimate status symbol.
53% of consumers cite durability as a key factor in determining a brand’s premiumness–which makes it the #1 most important attribute, ranking higher than craftsmanship, reputation, and even price.
48% say durability is also a key factor in evaluating brand value—again making it the #1 factor and beating out price, convenience, and authenticity.
The message is clear: People aren’t just buying products—they’re investing in longevity. Whether it’s a jacket, a car, or a piece of software, they want to know it will stand the test of time. If your brand delivers lasting quality, don’t just state it—prove it. Durability isn’t a nice-to-have; it’s the new benchmark for luxury and value.
The Number One Predictor of Loyalty? Vibes.
If the data tells us that consumers crave reliability, trust, and proof of performance, does that mean emotional connection no longer matters? Not at all. While people want rational assurances—quality, consistency, and longevity—there remains the deeply human desire to feel understood. It’s not just about finding the best brand; it’s about finding the brand that feels the most like them.
A brand’s “intuitive fit with my preferences/lifestyle” is the #1 predictor of both brand loyalty and affinity—ranking higher than price, convenience, customer service, or even “coolness.”
This sense of fit is deeply intangible. It’s not just about demographics or rational benefits—it’s about tone, aesthetics, values, and a brand’s overall energy. Consumers can instantly feel when a brand aligns with them, and they can just as quickly sense when it’s trying too hard.
The takeaway? Define your audience boldly, but more importantly, stay true to yourself. The brands that resonate most don’t force alignment—they create it by being unapologetically distinct. If you stand for something real, the right people will recognize it.
Survey Details: Nationwide online survey, 2,057 respondents, ages 18-78, demographically balanced across gender, ethnicity, region, education, and income.

# The Insights That Should Drive Every Campaign in 2025

As consumers navigate a world defined by instability, economic swings, and an endless barrage of information, they’re becoming more selective than ever. Skepticism is at an all-time high, and the brands that break through aren’t the ones making the most noise—they’re the ones proving, time and again, that they’re worth believing in.

With 2025 already shaping up to be another year of volatility, we partnered with leading survey platform Centiment to uncover the factors driving purchasing decisions in this new landscape. The findings reveal a fundamental shift: people are over chasing trends—they’re gravitating toward brands that offer consistency, authenticity, and real value.

For those looking to build deeper connections with their audience, these insights decode the psychology behind consumer trust—and how to earn it.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/6q3eaif3/production/4f23b39ec6f58fa71e9fd2aceb0ae8513b0a75a8-2560x1593.png?fm=webp&w=3840&q=75)

## The Reliability Revolution

Uncertainty has fundamentally rewired consumer psychology. In a world that feels increasingly unstable, people are clinging to what they know and trust. Our data paints a clear picture:

*   **74%** trust product claims from established businesses more than newer companies
*   **60%** prefer brands that refine existing offerings rather than constantly launching new ones
*   **61%** believe older businesses are more likely to genuinely care about their best interests than younger businesses
*   Even in a category like technology, only about half (**52%**) of consumers crave innovation

Consumers are done chasing the next big thing—they’re doubling down on brands with a track record of reliability. That means businesses should shift focus from chasing hype to reinforcing their existing value. Highlight longevity, consistency, and proof of performance. **Show customers that you're not just here today—you’ll be here tomorrow.**

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/6q3eaif3/production/29ff427394f9cedde7dc8ddcdc4373c7da7906fe-2560x1593.png?fm=webp&w=3840&q=75)

## You’re Wrong About GenZ

Growing up in an era of constant hype has made Gen Z naturally skeptical. They don’t just question marketing claims—**they can see trendiness itself as a red flag**. Compared to older generations, Gen Z is:

*   **10 percentage points** more likely to associate trendiness with low quality
*   **12 pp** more likely to associate trendiness with insincerity
*   **9 pp** more likely to associate trendiness with being overpriced
*   **8 pp** more likely to associate trendiness with being impractical
*   **15 pp** LESS likely to associate trendiness with innovation

The lesson? Chasing the latest TikTok trend won’t win Gen Z over; trust will. Instead of trying to be “of the moment,” focus on building real credibility. Show them **why your brand matters beyond the hype**, and how it stands for something deeper than just what’s trending today.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/6q3eaif3/production/b1a113220328e4cd33e7a5e2d82d3938fe8c1fd0-2560x1593.png?fm=webp&w=3840&q=75)

## Durability: The New Premium

Premium is no longer about price—it’s about staying power. Consumers are redefining what makes a brand feel high-end or worth their money, and **durability is now the ultimate status symbol.**

*   **53%** of consumers cite durability as a key factor in determining a brand’s premiumness–which makes it the #1 most important attribute, ranking higher than craftsmanship, reputation, and even price.
*   **48%** say durability is also a key factor in evaluating brand value—again making it the #1 factor and beating out price, convenience, and authenticity.

The message is clear: People aren’t just buying products—**they’re investing in longevity**. Whether it’s a jacket, a car, or a piece of software, they want to know it will stand the test of time. If your brand delivers lasting quality, don’t just state it—prove it. Durability isn’t a nice-to-have; it’s the new benchmark for luxury and value.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/6q3eaif3/production/92d5c1a92ffff214d317b6f3c8abfb5e16e3b854-2560x1593.png?fm=webp&w=3840&q=75)

## The Number One Predictor of Loyalty? Vibes.

If the data tells us that consumers crave reliability, trust, and proof of performance, does that mean emotional connection no longer matters? Not at all. While people want rational assurances—quality, consistency, and longevity—**there remains the deeply human desire to feel understood**. It’s not just about finding the best brand; it’s about finding the brand that **feels the most like them.**

*   A brand’s **“intuitive fit with my preferences/lifestyle”** is the **#1 predictor** of both brand loyalty and affinity—ranking higher than price, convenience, customer service, or even “coolness.”

**This sense of fit is deeply intangible.** It’s not just about demographics or rational benefits—it’s about tone, aesthetics, values, and a brand’s overall _energy._ Consumers can instantly feel when a brand aligns with them, and they can just as quickly sense when it’s trying too hard.

The takeaway? **Define your audience boldly, but more importantly, stay true to yourself.** The brands that resonate most don’t force alignment—they create it by being unapologetically distinct. If you stand for something real, the right people will recognize it.

_**Survey Details:** Nationwide online survey, 2,057 respondents, ages 18-78, demographically balanced across gender, ethnicity, region, education, and income._
